content.thinking:
I need to write the whole file carefully in one pass without verification, using the known builder API and relative imports. I'm designing a phoenix with spread wings standing on a rock so it touches the floor.

I'm sizing the phoenix at roughly 1.2m tall with a 3.6m wingspan, legs reaching the ground on a flat stone plinth, with the body swept along a path from chest to tail base, a long trailing tail, and neck rising to the head. For the wings, I'm planning arm bones sweeping from shoulder to wrist to tip, with primary feathers built as fanned extruded leaf shapes oriented along the wing plane.

Figuring out feather orientation math...

Now I'm defining the feather outline shape with a leaf-like curve and planning a color gradient from gold at the root through orange and red toward the tip.

For glow effects, since painted materials can't glow directly, I'll add separate glowing elements for the eyes, chest ember gem, and tail-tip flame cards. I'm also figuring out the feather layout for each wing: primaries, secondaries, and covert rows, each rooted at specific shoulder and wrist points with outward-angled placement.

Mapping feather roots along the wing arm path...

Checking wingspan against body size, the reach seems too large so I'm scaling down the primary length and height slightly to keep proportions balanced around 4.4m span. I'm adding shorter covert feathers in gold along the arm in layered rows, offsetting each row slightly in height to avoid z-fighting between coplanar feathers.

Now I'm counting total feather parts across the wing sections and planning the tail plumes as tapered sweeps rather than flat extrusions, using curved paths from the tail base outward with varying spread angles and lengths, and defining an elliptical radius function to taper each plume's cross-section along its length.

I'm also planning small gold eye-spot ellipsoids placed along each tail plume path at a fixed parameter, and sketching the body/neck as a single sweep through a sequence of catmull points from tail base up through chest to neck.

For radii I'm using a tapering five-key array, then shading the body paint with a cel-shaded fur-edge effect that switches between red and gold based on surface normal, wrapped for cartoon-style lighting before moving on to the breast feather cards.

Now I'm scattering flame-feather textured cards across the body surface using an SVG gradient, limiting coverage to the lower belly area, then building the head with a small sphere, a spiked gold beak, and amber anime-style eyes decaled onto the head surface.

For the crest, I'm planning five curved plumes sweeping back from the top of the head using catmull curves, tapering outward and upward.

For the neck ruff, I'm thinking about scattering feather cards around the neck by filtering the body scatter points to just the upper region near the head.

Now I'm working out the leg geometry, sweeping a catmull curve from thigh through knee to ankle with tapering radius, then considering feathery trouser coverage over the thigh.

I'm adding toe spikes with dark talon tips, positioning the plinth lathe shape so feet land properly on top of it, and sketching the base stone disc outline coordinates.

For the plinth itself, I'm giving it a mottled charred-stone coloring with ember cracks, plus a glowing orange rim ring and rising flame plumes along the sides to suggest embers around the base.

I'm adding glowing flame-card accents at the tail tip and wing primary tips, orienting each card frame to face upward at the feather points using a frame helper, with a layered teardrop flame texture for the glow effect.

Now I'm planning a chest gem — a small glowing gold sphere with a thin torus ring around it positioned on the front of the body — plus a gold filigree collar sweeping around the neck using a closed curved path.

Actually, I can use body.at(t) to grab the exact position, tangent, and interpolated radius along the path at that point, then scale neck rings proportionally to the body's local radius there — more robust than hardcoding positions. I'll apply the same approach for anklet rings on the legs.

I'm deciding to skip most tassel and plume accessories to keep things simple, but I'll add a small forehead gem using an octahedron geometry as a decorative touch on the head. Settling on a flat color palette — red, orange, gold, cream, dark maroon — for a clean stylized look, and planning to keep everything typed strictly in TypeScript.

Now I'm writing a feather helper function that builds each feather from a root point and direction vector, computing orthogonal axes to orient the feather plane correctly — being careful with the edge case where the direction vector points nearly straight up, since the cross-product math breaks down there.

No mirroring colour issues then. I'm defining the extrude call with position, direction vectors, and thickness for the feather outline, built from a set of corner points scaled by length and width with corner smoothing applied, keeping the tip sharp while rounding the other points.

Now I'm designing the paint function to color each feather based on normalized position along its length, blending through a gradient of stops while adding shading from surface normals, plus special cases for a bright golden tip and a pale shaft line down the center. I'm planning the color stops for different palettes, like a dark-red-to-gold gradient for a fiery theme.

Writing wing-building code...

Still working out feather angles...

Adding glow flame cards at primary tips, collecting their positions for the flame effect, and mirroring everything across the x-axis. I'm also offsetting feather root heights slightly per row to avoid z-fighting, and wiring up the body sweep surface with its paint function.

Now I'm figuring out decal targeting for the head's eyes, then working out the tail plumes—nine of them spreading symmetrically, with the middle plume longest and each tapering in width and curving down toward the tail tip while staying above the floor.

Still writing plume code...

Writing flame SVG texture...

I'm adding a seeded rng helper for scattering card hits, then planning ~14 glowing ember spheres near the plinth plus ten flame cards arranged in a ring facing upward. I'm tallying part counts across wings, cards, and tail spots to confirm everything stays within budget, and checking the sweep function's call signature.

I'm sketching out the surface scatter options (count, rng, min distance, filter) and the imports I'll need from the builder, path, frame, texture, and paint modules, including a custom ramp function for mapping positions to colors.

For the eye decals, I'm placing amber irises on the head using spherical coordinates around a head center point, with decals sized small and positioned via hit testing before finishing up the module's exports.

Now I'm structuring the phoenix builder function, placing wing joints (shoulder, elbow, wrist, hand) with increasing x-offset and height to create a sweeping wing shape, giving roughly 5.2m wingspan and proper body/wing proportions. I'm also setting up a tapering arm radius profile and coloring with a cel-shaded red tone.

I'm defining a feather function with root position, direction, length, width, and paint parameters, computing a perpendicular vector for feather orientation by crossing against an up-tilted normal. I'm adding a small gold claw spike at the wrist, and finishing with fanned covert plumes at the tail base.
